subject: general
question: Insects breathe through:
solution:
The correct answer is__** spiracles.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Insects breathe through **spiracles**, which are small openings located on the sides of their bodies.
 
• These spiracles lead to a network of **tracheae** that deliver oxygen directly to the tissues.
 
• Spiracles help in the exchange of gases, allowing oxygen in and carbon dioxide out.
 
• Insects do not have lungs; instead, they rely on this system of spiracles and tracheae for respiration.
 
• The tracheal system is highly efficient, enabling insects to thrive in various environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spiracles**: These are external openings that connect to the tracheal system, facilitating gas exchange in insects.
 
• **Tracheal System**: A network of tubes that transport oxygen directly to the cells and tissues, allowing for efficient respiration without the need for blood circulation of oxygen.
 
• **Lungs**: Found in vertebrates, lungs are not present in insects. They use spiracles instead to breathe.
 
• **Gills**: Aquatic organisms like fish use gills for respiration, but insects primarily rely on spiracles.
 
• **Skin Respiration**: Some organisms can breathe through their skin, but this is not a primary method for insects.
